Week 1–3 exposed confounders: resetting to original pretrained OPT differs from resetting to real-trained S0; five epochs executed differed from selecting epoch 1. Repeating the WikiText real set alone raised test PPL from 33.89 to 84.56 over ten five-epoch cycles, with falling training loss. We then matched fresh/repeated real/synthetic continuations on FineWeb. The table reports completed OPT/AdamW/cosine outcomes, not the newer SGD experiment. Repeated synthetic means regenerated targets each epoch. Higher PPL means poorer prediction of real held-out text; it alone cannot uniquely identify collapse or overfitting.

The current experiments use pretrained SmolLM2-135M and a separate native-tokenizer FineWeb-Edu bank. Ten fresh, document-disjoint chunks of 10,000 pairs. A pair contains 64 real prompt tokens and 64 continuation tokens. BOS plus both gives 129 input positions; prompt attention stays active, but only the 64 continuation tokens contribute to loss. Every condition uses identical prompts and held-out real continuations. Synthetic targets come from that condition’s preceding checkpoint and are frozen before training. Independent arms start from identical original pretrained weights. Full test = 7,303 pairs / 467,392 scored targets. SmolLM2 pretraining includes FineWeb-Edu, so experimental separation is not proof of pretraining novelty.

The previous AdamW/cosine sweeps motivated a simpler recipe. This is not an optimizer-only causal comparison: optimizer, LR schedule, regularization, precision and decoding changed together. Within the new sweep only target fraction changes. SGD LR 0.01 was selected using the recorded bounded real-only calibration, not test or synthetic outcomes. No momentum, weight decay, clipping, warm-up or scheduler. FP32 with TF32 disabled. Seed 42, microbatch 32 and effective batch 128; 79 updates per cycle including a final 16-example batch, 790 per arm. Greedy deterministic generation, exactly 64 new tokens, repetition penalty 1.0.

The real curve reports the ratio of mean source-weighted loss terms across all 79 updates in each cycle, including tails. At cycle 10 it is 49.08766794%; token-weighting all examples instead gives 47.4622%. Do not confuse this scalar loss share with gradient share or beneficial influence. Cycle-10 source mean NLLs are about 5.333 real and 0.0596 synthetic: the model confidently predicts many of its own targets, while real continuations remain surprising. Real rows are 1% over the epoch, not necessarily in every batch. This observation motivates measuring actual gradients and held-out consequences.

40 seconds.

For equal 64-target examples, L_R = (1/B) sum over real rows of their mean continuation NLL, with the analogous synthetic term. Source proportions are already in those terms. Gradient vectors add: g = grad L_R + grad L_S. The plotted norm of their sum is not the sum of norms. SGD subtracts 0.01 times the combined gradient. Finally, unseen-real loss depends on direction and local curvature, not just training loss or vector magnitude. Nearly half the loss does not mean nearly half the gradient or accuracy gain.

At each original SGD update, measure a fixed 128-pair real-validation probe using temporary copies from identical preupdate tensors. Q_M is the actual mixed update, Q_S synthetic alone, Q_R real alone. Real conditional effect = NLL(Q_M)-NLL(Q_S); synthetic conditional effect = NLL(Q_M)-NLL(Q_R). Below zero improves probe predictions. Real inclusion helps all 563 updates containing real examples. Synthetic inclusion worsens 778/790 in this 99% trajectory. Curves are means across all 79 updates including zero real contributions in absent-source batches. Effects do not add because of nonlinear interaction. Probe results are not complete-test PPL and no held-out gradients train the model.

Conclude with measured scope. Self-generated deterministic targets become easy, leaving little training loss while real targets remain informative. Real inclusion produces a beneficial local held-out effect; whole-epoch source removal reinforces that directional explanation in the selected cases. This is not a universal threshold, permanent stabilization or proof of a stationary point. Tail batches and order matter, especially at 99%. New seeds, longer runs, fixed-size tail handling and stochastic decoding are the next controlled tests. Existing checkpoints, configurations, exact data/provenance and analyses are saved in the repository and private recovery storage.

Distinct-2/3 pool unique token ngrams divided by all within-output ngram occurrences across256 outputs. Denominators256*63 and256*62. A lower value indicates fewer unique phrases across the collection; not necessarily more repetition in each output. Pooled token entropy can rise while within-output repetition worsens because topic/vocabulary variation between outputs differs from repetition within one. These are greedy probe outputs, not model predictive entropy or factual accuracy.
